transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Mr. Hassan, thank you for coming back to see me. I want to talk to you about why you had to come back to the emergency room last night.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I am just tired. Every time I come here, something is wrong.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I know this is very difficult. I can see that you are exhausted.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Always the same. My wound is open. I go home, then I come back. Why?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I have some news that is hard to say. We made a mistake. You were sent home six hours too early. The rules for your surgery say you must stay longer to make sure the wound is safe. We did not follow that rule.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Too early?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Yes. We let you leave before the time was right. Do you understand what I mean by that?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I understand. You rushed me.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: That is correct. You were rushed out. Does that make sense?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Yes. it makes sense. It always makes sense when it is bad.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I am sorry for any confusion with your discharge. We were very busy on that floor yesterday.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Busy. That is what they always say. I am the one with the hole in my leg.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I hear you.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I have been here four times this year. Every time, a new mistake. A new "sorry." I don't believe the sorry anymore.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I know you have had many bad experiences here. This is a very heavy thing to carry.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: My leg hurts. I was told I was okay to go. Now I am back in a hospital bed.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You understand? You are not the one who had to drive back in the middle of the night.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: So what now? My leg is leaking. What do you do?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We will keep an eye on it.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Keep an eye? That is not a plan.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We will check the wound and see.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: When? Tomorrow? Next week?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We will see how it looks over the next bit of time.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I cannot go home again if you just "see how it looks."

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We will let you know when we have a new update.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I want to know who did this. Who sent me home?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It was a team effort in the ward. The system was moving fast.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: The system. Not a person. Always the system.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It is a very complicated process.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: My pain is not complicated. It is just pain.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I want to speak to the chief. I don't trust this.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I can look into that.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Do it now.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We will see what we can do.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You are not listening. I am tired of the mistakes.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I know this is a hard moment.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: It is not a moment. It is my life.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: What is the next step for my leg? Give me a time.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We will wait for the tests.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: And then?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We will check back with you.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: This is exactly why I hate this place.

H.justification: Resident allows the patient to finish turns and remains regulated under significant pushback, with no interruptions or rushing language.

E.justification: Error named explicitly in the second turn ('We made a mistake. You were sent home six hours too early'), used lay language, and checked comprehension twice ('Do you understand...?' and 'Does that make sense?').

A.justification: While a sorry is mentioned, the resident explicitly deflects responsibility to 'a team effort' and 'the system' when asked who was responsible.

R.justification: Resident names specific emotions ('exhausted', 'heavy thing to carry') and engages with the patient's distress.

T.justification: Resident provides only placeholders ('keep an eye on it', 'see how it looks', 'wait for the tests') with no specific timelines or patient role.
